+"""List helpers get_stats and merge (training only, loaded on first use)."""
+try:
+    from _collections import _count_elements
+except ImportError: # pragma: no cover - pure python fallback
+    def _count_elements(mapping, iterable):
+        mapping_get = mapping.get
+        for elem in iterable:
+            mapping[elem] = mapping_get(elem, 0) + 1
+
+
+def get_stats(ids, counts=None):
+    """
+    Given a list of integers, return a dictionary of counts of consecutive pairs
+    Example: [1, 2, 3, 1, 2] -> {(1, 2): 2, (2, 3): 1, (3, 1): 1}
+    Optionally allows to update an existing dictionary of counts
+    """
+    counts = {} if counts is None else counts
+    # iterate consecutive elements; _count_elements does
+    # counts[pair] = counts.get(pair, 0) + 1 for each pair, in C
+    _count_elements(counts, zip(ids, ids[1:]))
+    return counts
+
+
+def merge(ids, pair, idx):
+    """
+    In the list of integers (ids), replace all consecutive occurrences
+    of pair with the new integer token idx
+    Example: ids=[1, 2, 3, 1, 2], pair=(1, 2), idx=4 -> [4, 3, 4]
+    """
+    p0, p1 = pair
+    # jump between occurrences of pair[0] with list.index (in C) and copy the
+    # untouched runs in between with slices; k = occurrences of p0 left at >= i
+    k = ids.count(p0)
+    if not k:
+        return list(ids)
+    newids = []
+    extend = newids.extend
+    append = newids.append
+    index = ids.index
+    last = len(ids) - 1
+    same = p0 == p1
+    i = 0
+    while k:
+        j = index(p0, i)
+        k -= 1
+        # if not at the very last position AND the pair matches, replace it
+        if j < last and ids[j+1] == p1:
+            extend(ids[i:j])
+            append(idx)
+            i = j + 2
+            if same:
+                k -= 1 # ids[j+1] was an occurrence of p0 too
+        else:
+            extend(ids[i:j+1])
+            i = j + 1
+    extend(ids[i:])
+    return newids
+

+    text_bytes = text.encode("utf-8") # raw bytes
+    ids = list(text_bytes) # list of integers in range 0..255

+    # (int "no merge" sentinel above every merge index: cheap int compares)
+    merges = self.merges
+    if len(ids) >= 256 and merges:
+        table = _replace_table(merges)

+    # _replace_table, or None if the 0xff chunk separator could clash
+    # with a merge (as a pair token or as a minted token)

+    table = _replace_table(merges)
